Formulation
- Predisposing factors: Type 2 diabetes (may affect skin integrity); history of generalized dry skin.
- Precipitating factors: Change of job ~4 months ago with increased exposure to cleaning agents.
- Perpetuating factors: Inconsistent glove use at work, inadequate skin hydration measures (previous emollient use was ineffective), scratching leading to occasional bleeding, ongoing occupational exposure.
- Protective factors: Patient is engaged with care, agreed to prescribed treatment and to use gloves; has access to pharmacy for prescription.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Dermatitis / probable contact dermatitis of the palms
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce pain, itching, cracking of hands.
  - Restore ability to perform work duties without interruption.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Reduce inflammation and skin breakdown within 10–14 days.
  - Prevent recurrence by reducing exposure to triggers and improving skin care.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Wear protective gloves during all cleaning activities.
  - Apply emollients (as instructed) 3–4 times daily.
  - Use prescribed steroid cream as directed (name/dose/frequency to be on prescription).
  - Return for review if no improvement within 10–14 days or sooner if symptoms worsen or spread.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescribe topical steroid cream — name/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript (prescription to be sent to pharmacy).
  - Prescribe stronger emollient(s) — name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Advise avoidance of triggers and consistent glove use at work.
  - Arrange follow-up review in approximately 10–14 days or earlier if worsening.

Secondary Problem: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Not recorded (no diabetes-specific goals discussed).
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Not recorded (no diabetes-specific plans discussed in this consult).
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue current diabetes medication (Metformin) as previously prescribed — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):

Tertiary Problem: Occupational exposure / work impairment
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Minimize exposure to irritants and return to work full duties.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Reduce occupational dermatitis and prevent future episodes.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Consistently wear gloves while cleaning.
  - Report to employer if workplace accommodations are needed (not documented whether done).
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide advice on avoidance of triggers and appropriate skin care.
  - Support with documentation for occupational health or work excuse if requested (not documented that provided).

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Likely diagnosis: dermatitis/contact dermatitis.
  - Avoidance of triggers: wear gloves while cleaning.
  - Topical treatment: steroid cream recommended (details to be on prescription).
  - Emollient use: apply stronger emollient 3–4 times daily.
  - Expected timeframe: improvement expected in approximately 10–14 days.
  - Return instructions: come back sooner if spreading or worsening.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Spreading of rash, increasing dryness/cracking, worsening pain, increased bleeding from scratching.
- Coping Strategies:
  - Protective measures (glove use); regular emollient use; seek earlier review if symptoms worsen.
